resources.string: Private email alerts through your chosen push service.
Choose a UnifiedPush app, such as ntfy, installed on this phone.
Notifications are off for MailPush. Allow them to see email alerts.
Choose a push service, then add a signed-in email account. You will pair it with the connector running alongside Proton Mail Bridge.
Bridge and the connector must stay running to send alerts.

Alerts are encrypted between your connector and this phone. The push module does not receive your Proton password or mail decryption keys.

Notification private keys are protected with Android Keystore. Alerts say “You have new mail” unless you enable sender and subject previews for an account. Proton Mail uses its own connection to download your mail.

The push service can still see delivery timing and IP addresses. Bridge and the connector must remain running.
Secure storage is unavailable. Your existing data has been preserved. Restart the phone and try again. Reinstalling would require pairing again.
Waiting for the first encrypted alert. Send a test from the connector to check delivery.
Email details can appear in notifications, even while the mail app is locked. Off by default.

Previews show the sender and subject supplied by your connector. Enable preview = true in the connector configuration as well as this switch.

Details are decrypted on this phone and shared with Android notifications, including while Proton Mail is locked. Android lock-screen privacy settings still apply.

Turning previews off clears the current alerts for this account. New alerts will use “You have new mail”.
Could not finish changing the preview setting. Refresh the status and check your choice.
Waiting for the push service to register this account. Keep the selected push app running, then try again.
Save the encrypted request file, then import it with mailpush pair on your connector. The next screen shows your one-time pairing key.
Use your request file and one-time key in the connector. Then import the encrypted .receipt file it creates.
Create a fresh encrypted request and finish pairing with the connector again. Your current pairing stays in place until a verified new receipt is imported.
This deletes the local pairing and notification keys for these alerts. Your email account stays signed in. Revoke this device on the connector too if you will no longer use it.
Install a UnifiedPush distributor, such as the Google-free ntfy app, then return here to choose it.
Existing accounts may need pairing again because their delivery endpoints will change.
Could not select the push service. Try opening that app, then choose it again.
Sign in to an email account in Proton Mail before setting up alerts.
Use the same IDs as your connector configuration. For one mailbox, the default is personal. Separate multiple IDs with commas.
Leave empty unless your provider requires it
Most setups do not need this. Only enter the public key supplied by your push provider.
Use a valid 87-character VAPID public key, or leave this empty.
Use 1–32 mailbox IDs containing letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens (up to 48 characters each).
Could not save this alert setup. Your existing accounts have been preserved.
Registration failed. Open the selected push service, then try reconnecting.
Could not create an encrypted pairing request. Try again without removing your account.
This request has expired. Create and save a new pairing request.

Enter this key in the hidden prompt shown by mailpush pair on your connector. Keep it separate from the encrypted request file. Compare the fingerprint, then import the returned receipt to finish pairing.
Could not read the pairing key. Create a fresh request if the problem continues.
Pairing complete. Send an encrypted test from the connector to check delivery.
The pairing file could not be verified. Check that you selected the matching .receipt file, or create a fresh request.
Could not remove this alert setup. Try again after restarting the phone.
